Macrons

Consonantal i

Body, health & movement

yawn verb and noun

also yawning, gape

classical

1ōscitō: long o (Lewis & Short oscĭto, leaving the o unmarked). The related noun ōs, ōris n., mouth, has a long ō.

ōscitō1, ōscitāre, ōscitāvī, ōscitātum

verb, first conjugation

yawn or gape

The deponent ōscitor, ōscitārī, ōscitātus sum is also attested.

Examples

  • Theodōrus ōscitat.

    Theo is yawning.composed

Other words

  • ōscitātiō, ōscitātiōnis f. — yawning, a yawn

    noun, third declension · classical

  • ōscitāns, ōscitantis — yawning

    also used · classical

See also mouth, stretch.

SourcesLewis & Short: oscito · Lewis & Short: oscitatio

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
